# From Convenience to Compliance: How Regulations Are Reshaping Consumer Wipes


Regulatory developments are becoming an increasingly important driver of wipes innovation. At[OUTLOOK™ 2026](https://www.edana.org/events/outlook/outlook-2026) ,[Elisabeth Swennenhuis](https://www.linkedin.com/in/els-swennenhuis-203612/) , Product Line Manager, Consumer Wipes at Magnera, will discuss how regulations such as the[Single-Use Plastics Directive (SUPD),](https://environment.ec.europa.eu/topics/plastics/single-use-plastics_en) Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) schemes, environmental claims legislation, and emerging circular economy policies are influencing product development and shaping the future of the wipes market.


## Consumer Wipes Are Evolving


[Consumer wipes](https://magnera.com/market/wipes/) have traditionally been defined by performance attributes such as softness, strength, convenience, and efficacy. While those expectations remain, manufacturers now face additional pressures from evolving regulations, sustainability goals, and increasing demands for transparency.


Today’s product developers must consider not only performance and manufacturability, but also labeling requirements, environmental claims, material traceability, and emerging circular economy initiatives. As a result, material selection has become a strategic product development decision rather than simply a sourcing choice.


## The Challenge of Balancing Performance and Compliance


No substrate can optimize every performance characteristic. Improvements in one area often require trade-offs in another. For example, increasing strength may affect softness, while higher absorbency can influence liquid release properties or converting efficiency.


Beyond performance considerations, manufacturers must also evaluate how material choices may impact future regulatory compliance and product claims. Regulatory preparedness is increasingly becoming part of the product design process from the earliest stages of development.


## Collaboration Drives Better Outcomes


As innovation becomes more complex, collaboration across the value chain is essential. Material suppliers can provide technical expertise, testing capabilities, and regulatory insights that help manufacturers evaluate alternatives, reduce risk, and accelerate development timelines.


By considering performance, manufacturability, and compliance together, organizations can make more informed decisions and position products for long-term success.


## Looking Ahead


The wipes market continues to evolve as consumer expectations, regulations, and sustainability objectives grow increasingly interconnected. Manufacturers that integrate regulatory awareness alongside material science and product performance will be better positioned to adapt to changing market requirements and future policy developments.
